column1: # Civil clocks kept at particular places before 1970, for each year
# researched, including years that match the time-zone database's record.
# Generated from a research register; never edited by hand.
# One row per interval, per place, per researched year. Each researched year
# is covered whole, from 00:00 on 1 January to 00:00 on 1 January of the next
# year, by intervals that abut: each row's `from` is the text of the previous
# row's `to`. Rows are sorted by geonameid, then by `from`.
# Columns: lat, lon (the place's coordinates exactly as the atlas gives them:
# the key); geonameid, name (a record of the place, not its key); zone (the
# zone the place is cast in); from, to (local date and time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM);
# offset (from UT, as -06:00); abbreviation; kind; source_ids (the sources of
# the place's year, separated by ';', the same list on each of its rows).
#   kind clock      the place kept this offset;
#   kind disputed   the sources do not settle which clock was kept; offset
#                   and abbreviation are empty.
# Ends. Each `from` and `to` is read on the clock in force before that
# instant: the offset of the interval that ends there (a change to summer
# time is at its hour of standard time, a return at its hour of summer time).
# Where the interval that ends there is disputed, the instant is read on the
# clock of the interval that begins there. A place's first `from` is read on
# its own interval's clock. Midnight at the end of a day is written as 00:00
# of the next day.
# A year for which a place has no rows is one the research has not settled:
# the time-zone database's record stands for it. The first `from` after such a
# year is read on its own interval's clock.
# An instant with a disputed interval on one side and no row on the other is
# read on the first clock after it at that place, or, where none follows, on
# the last clock before it.
# Disputed intervals that meet are written as one row, which may run across
# the end of a year; its source_ids are those of every year it covers.
# Where another place has exactly the coordinates of a place here, the clocks
# given at those coordinates are the researched place's.
lat
